title: Xcode builds: configurations, schemes and faster build times
summary: Targets build products, configurations (Debug/Release/Staging) change settings, schemes choose what to build, run and test. Build time is a team-wide productivity cost worth measuring and fixing.
body: **Vocabulary:** **Project** contains **targets** (app, extensions, tests, frameworks). **Build configuration** = a set of build settings (Debug: no optimization, Release: optimized). **Scheme** = which targets to build and which configuration to use for Run/Test/Archive. **xcconfig** files hold build settings as text (reviewable in PRs, fewer merge conflicts).
**Environments:** Staging vs Production via configurations or schemes with different bundle IDs, API URLs and app icons; read values from Info.plist set by xcconfig. Keep secrets out of the repo.
**Dependencies:** Swift Package Manager is the standard now; CocoaPods is in maintenance mode; Carthage is rare. Pin versions and review updates.

**Faster builds:** modularize so changes rebuild less; avoid huge files and complex type inference (add explicit types in long expressions); use `-warn-long-function-bodies` and Build Timeline to find slow code; prefer static linking; cache builds on CI; avoid unnecessary Run Script phases (or mark their inputs/outputs).
**Explicit modules / build caching:** newer Xcode versions build modules explicitly and can cache compilation, improving incremental and CI builds.
**Staff angle:** track clean and incremental build time and CI duration as team metrics; one slow build × 100 engineers × 20 builds a day is a lot of lost time.
keyPoints: Target = product; configuration = settings set; scheme = what/how to build-run-test.
Use xcconfig files for reviewable settings and environment separation.
SPM is the default dependency manager.
Speed up builds: modularize, explicit types in heavy expressions, Build Timeline, CI caching.
Measure build time as a productivity metric.

code.caption: xcconfig for environments

mistakes: Using `#if DEBUG` everywhere for environment switching instead of configurations.
Run scripts without declared inputs/outputs that run on every build.
followups: **Why is my incremental build slow?** A widely imported module changed, a script phase runs every time, or heavy type-checking; check the Build Timeline.
**Why `$()` in the URL?** `//` starts a comment in xcconfig files; `$()` breaks it up.
